artworks.title: Priam Asking Achilles for the Body of Hector
artworks.description: Ivanov's tent — Priam kissing Achilles' hands for Hector's body, Iliad XXIV as Russian neoclassical mercy.

artworks.title: Priam Pleading with Achilles for the Body of Hector
artworks.description: Hamilton's ransom — the old king pleading before the seated hero, the poem's quietest and greatest scene of pity.

artworks.title: Priam at the Feet of Achilles
artworks.description: Langlois' Priam at Achilles' feet — the ransom that ends the Iliad not with Troy's fall but with shared grief.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Peter O'Toole's Priam kneels in Achilles' tent — the ransom of Hector restaged as the film's quietest mercy.

popCulture.title: Priam
popCulture.description: The old king who kisses the hands that killed his sons — Book XXIV's ransom remains antiquity's great scene of pity.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.description: The poem ends not with Troy's fall but with shared grief over Hector's body — Priam and Achilles at one table.
